title: Animal Bite
portraitNote: Match subway-afro-dandy likeness: young Black man, large heart-shaped afro, calm direct gaze, light blue hospital gown on ED stretcher. Forearm animal bite wound with surrounding cellulitis visible where appropriate. Same face and afro silhouette throughout — clinical stress, trauma bay.
correct_orders: Stabilize the patient: ensure airway, breathing, and circulatory status
Obtain a complete blood count (CBC) and serum glucose level
Culture and debridement of the wound if appropriate
Consult Infectious Disease specialist for potential rabies prophylaxis
should_avoid: Initiate antibiotics prior to culture results due to risk of developing antibiotic-resistant infections

rationale.Stabilize the patient: Primary survey — airway, breathing, circulation before wound-specific care.
rationale.Stabilize the patient: ensure airway, br: Primary survey — airway, breathing, circulation before wound-specific care.
rationale.Administer tetanus prophylaxis if needed: Wound prophylaxis channel — separate from ABC stabilization; both required for animal bites.
rationale.Obtain CBC and serum glucose level: To monitor for infection or complications
rationale.Culture and debridement of the wound: To diagnose potential infections and remove necrotic tissue
rationale.Consult Infectious Disease specialist: For potential rabies prophylaxis if the animal cannot be traced or if it is a known rabid animal
rationale.Initiate antibiotics prior to culture re: Avoidance due to risk of developing antibiotic-resistant infections
rationale.Oxygen: To provide supplemental oxygen for the patient suffering from an animal bite, which can cause distress or airway obstruction.
rationale.IV access x2: For fluid and medication administration in case of severe infection or complications arising from the animal bite.

physical_exam: Animal Bite — exam tailored to chief complaint on arrival.
Soft, non-distended, no focal peritoneal signs on initial exam.
Alert and oriented unless perfusion or metabolic derangement present.
No acute rash; capillary refill and perfusion assessed.
